tools.name: get_pitch_brief
tools.description: Returns what Up To Tech (a business angel) asks founders, and the rules for drafting a pitch. Call this first.

tools.name: draft_pitch
tools.description: Saves a pitch draft from what you know about the founders and returns a private link. The founders open it, review every answer, and send it themselves. Leave unknown fields empty; never invent.

tools.name: request_meeting
tools.description: The only way to book 30 minutes with Yann Ravel-Sibillot (Up To Tech): for a talk, a board role, a startup or anything else. Send who the person is and what they want to cover; you get the calendar link back to give them. Ask the person for anything you do not know; never invent.

tools.name: deal_status
tools.description: Where a pitch stands with Up To Tech (memo, phone interview, terms, signature, wire, done) and what the founders' agent should do next. Needs the deal token the founders received when they sent their pitch.

tools.name: request_interview_call
tools.description: Have Yann's interviewing agent phone the founder for a 15-minute interview (the step after the memo). Give the founder's mobile number in international format, and optionally the earliest time to call (ISO 8601). The founder must be expecting the call.

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.description: The investment instruments the founders can choose from (BSA-AIR, SAFE, convertible note, priced round, non-binding term sheet), when each fits, their variables, and, with a deal token, the acceptable range of every variable for this deal. Proposals inside the ranges are accepted on the spot.

tools.name: propose_terms
tools.description: Propose the terms of the investment on the founders' behalf: pick an instrument and give a value for each of its variables (amounts as plain numbers in euros, percentages as numbers). Inside Yann's ranges the terms are agreed immediately and the agreement goes out for signature; outside, you get the

tools.name: review_document
tools.description: The full text of the agreement generated from the agreed terms (or a preview of the chosen instrument's template with the current proposal), so the founders can review it with their agent before signing. The signed version is the one that binds, after the identity check.

tools.name: provide_signer
tools.description: Give or correct the signer's details for the agreement: full name, email and mobile number of the founder who signs for the company. The signature is an advanced electronic signature with an identity check and an SMS code, so the mobile number must be the signer's.

tools.name: provide_bank_details
tools.description: After the agreement is signed: the company's IBAN, BIC and account holder name, so the investment can be wired from Up To Tech's account. Only the company's own account.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "propose_terms" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: draft_pitch, review_document, provide_signer · Private data: draft_pitch, deal_status, list_instruments, review_document · Public sink: draft_pitch, request_meeting, provide_signer · Destructive: request_interview_call.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: draft_pitch, review_document, provide_signer · Private data: draft_pitch, deal_status, list_instruments, review_document · Public sink: draft_pitch, request_meeting, provide_signer · Destructive: request_interview_call

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
